title: Only so many at once
description:
A `std::counting_semaphore` hands out a fixed number of permits. A thread must `acquire()` one before entering and `release()` it on the way out, so at most that many threads are ever inside together.

Write `int peakConcurrency(int workers, int permits)`.

It starts `workers` threads. Each one acquires a permit from a `std::counting_semaphore<>` created with `permits`, does a little "work" (sleep for 5 milliseconds), and releases the permit. While inside, each thread adds one to a shared count of threads currently working and takes one off when it leaves. The function returns the **highest** value that count ever reached.

Protect the current count and the peak with a `std::mutex` (lesson 12.02), since several threads update them. If the semaphore is doing its job, the result is never more than `permits`.
hints: Create `std::counting_semaphore<> gate{ permits };`, and in each thread: `gate.acquire();`, then under the mutex increase `inside` and raise `peak` if `inside` is now larger; sleep; under the mutex again decrease `inside`; `gate.release();`.

Keep each locked region short: a `std::scoped_lock lock{ countMutex };` inside its own pair of braces unlocks at the closing brace, so the sleep happens without holding the mutex. (Lesson 12.05 shows how `std::atomic` can do the same job without a mutex.)
lessonTitle: Condition Variables, Semaphores, Latches and Barriers
